title: Krull dimension of an arbitrary algebraic homogeneous quotient
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A$ be a separated group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $L\hookrightarrow A$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $A/L$ be the separated finite-type scheme representing the fpqc coset quotient, with its quotient morphism as in [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient]. Then the topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] satisfy $$\dim A=\dim L+\dim(A/L).$$ All three dimensions are finite nonnegative integers. No smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, normality or affineness assumption is imposed on $A$ or $L$.

source.place: Proposition 5.23, printed p.104, including its reduction to the associated reduced schemes and A.72.

proof.text: Put $X=A/L$ and write $q:A\to X$ for the supplied quotient. Its cited statement gives that $X$ is finite type over $k$ and $q$ is flat, surjective and finitely presented. The affine presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] shows directly that $q$ is locally of finite type. To check finite type of $L$, choose a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ of $A$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], its inverse images in $L$ are $\operatorname{Spec}(R_i/I_i)$; the images of any finite generating list of $R_i$ generate $R_i/I_i$. This is a finite affine cover of $L$, so $L$ is finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For each of $A,L,X$, the affine coordinate rings in such a cover are Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], so the schemes are locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Their global dimensions are finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. The identity sections give points of $A$ and $L$, and $q(e_A)$ gives a point of $X$. Thus none is empty and all three dimensions are nonnegative integers. Set $d=\dim L\in\mathbb N$.

source.place: Proposition 5.23; use the supplied quotient of Theorem 5.28 and Proposition 5.25. Affine Noetherian input: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00FN; finiteness: varieties.tex Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic).

proof.text:
Fix $a\in A$, put $x=q(a)$ and $K=\kappa(a)$, and let $g:\operatorname{Spec}K\to A$ be its canonical residue-field morphism. Put $v=qg$ and $F=A\times_{X,v}\operatorname{Spec}K$. This fibre product has a $K$-point $\widetilde g=(g,1)$. There is a pointed $K$-isomorphism
$$\phi:L_K=L\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K\longrightarrow F,\qquad h\longmapsto gh,$$
sending the identity to $\widetilde g$. Here is the complete inverse construction. Write $b:F\to A$ and $r:F\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ for the projections. Since $qb=qgr$, the quotient's test-scheme criterion, applied to $T=F$, says $(gr)^{-1}b$ factors through $j:L\hookrightarrow A$; the factor is unique because $j_T$ is injective. Together with $r$ it defines $\psi:F\to L_K$. Conversely the same criterion gives $q(gh)=q(g)$, so multiplication defines $\phi$ by the fibre-product universal property. The identities $g(g^{-1}b)=b$ and $g^{-1}(gh)=h$ show $\phi\psi=1$ and $\psi\phi=1$ by their projections and the injectivity of $j$. These are morphisms on the full schemes, including nilpotents.

source.place: Proposition 5.24: the explicit torsor identity, restricted along g; compare Proposition 5.27.

proof.text:
The base change $L_K$ is finite type over the field $K$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Pulling back the multiplication, identity and inverse diagrams gives its group-scheme structure. Apply the group specialization of [lem-sfb-field-groupoid-constant-local-dimension] at its identity: $\dim_{e}(L_K)=\dim L_K$. For a scheme the identity etale chart in that statement computes precisely the local topological dimension used here. Apply the field-extension clause of [lem-kun-dimension-extension] to the finite-type $k$-scheme $L$ to get $\dim L_K=\dim L=d$. The isomorphism $\phi$ of Step 2 gives a bijection of open neighbourhoods of the distinguished points and preserves their chains of irreducible closed subsets, hence
$$\dim_{\widetilde g}F=\dim_e L_K=d.$$
Only local topological dimensions occur in this equality; no dimension of a local ring is substituted for them.

source.place: Tag 06FE (lemma-group-over-field-locally-finite-type-dimension), clause (1); field extension: algebra.tex Tag 00P3; Milne Proposition 5.23.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to $q:A\to X$ and $v:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$, with the point $\widetilde g\in F$ over $a$. The base point in $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has residue field $K$, so the fibre of $F\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ over that point is $F$ itself. The cited equality therefore says
$$\dim_a(A_x)=\dim_{\widetilde g}F=d.$$
The hypothesis that $q$ is locally of finite type was checked in Step 1. Since $a$ was arbitrary, the ordinary fibres of $q$ have local topological dimension $d$ at every point. No rational lift over $\kappa(x)$ was assumed: the extension used is the actual residue field $\kappa(a)$.

source.place: Tag 02FY (lemma-dimension-fibre-after-base-change), clause (1), for the base change along v.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-surjective-flat-global-dimension] to $q:A\to X$ and $d=\dim L$. Its local Noetherian, flat and locally finite type hypotheses hold by Step 1, its constant pointwise fibre dimension hypothesis is Step 4, and its surjectivity and nonempty-base hypotheses hold by Step 1. It yields $\dim A=\dim X+d$. Commutativity of addition of the finite integers of Step 1 gives
$$\dim A=\dim L+\dim(A/L).$$
The finiteness and nonnegativity assertions were also proved in Step 1. Nothing in Steps 2--4 requires smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, normality or affineness of either group.
